output.population: Participants in 50 controlled trials of salt-reduction interventions, with no restriction by age, sex, or hypertension status in the systematic review.
output.intervention: Salt substitution, nutrition education, self-help materials, or food reformulation.
output.comparator: Control/comparator conditions within included controlled trials.
output.effect: Pooled eligible trials showed salt substitution reduced SBP by WMD -7.44 mmHg and DBP by -3.77 mmHg (both P<0.001), while nutrition education reduced SBP by -2.75 mmHg and DBP by -2.11 mmHg (both P<0.001). Self-help materials reduced SBP by -2.60 mmHg in ages 25-60 (P=0.008) and, among hypertensive participants, SBP by -3.87 mmHg (P=0.003) and DBP by -2.91 mmHg (P<0.001).
output.applicability_boundary: Applies to the controlled trials included in the review; effects differ by intervention type and subgroup, and the authors state further trials are required.
output.source_span: salt substitution and nutrition education interventions had significant effects on both SBP

uncertainties: The source notes that further trials are required.
